prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: Sentinel Vale is an Earth-observation mission intended to provide routine land, coastal, and cryosphere imaging products with predictable latency and documented data quality.
S002: The ground segment exists to plan spacecraft activities, acquire mission data, maintain safe spacecraft operations, generate user products, preserve mission records, and provide controlled access to services.
S003: This operational concept treats the spacecraft, launch segment, and external user processing environments as outside the ground segment boundary except where interfaces are required for operations.
S004: The ground segment boundary includes the Mission Control Center, Flight Dynamics Facility, Payload Processing Facility, Network Control System, Long Term Archive, User Services Portal, Mission Planning System, Command Validation Gateway, Telemetry Ingest Service, Orbit Determination Engine, Product Quality Service, Primary Processing Cluster, and Backup Processing Cluster.
S005: The boundary also includes the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna as controlled operational assets.
S006: For local voice coordination only, Mission Control Center is introduced in this document with the alias Bluebell.
S007: The Mission Control Center is the authority for real-time spacecraft operations, pass supervision, anomaly response, and release of validated command activities.
S008: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit analysis, maneuver planning support, access prediction, and navigation products required by other ground functions.
S009: The Payload Processing Facility provides the operational environment for payload data processing, calibration control, product assessment, and distribution staging.
S010: The Network Control System monitors communications availability, routes operational traffic, and provides status awareness for ground connectivity supporting the mission.
S011: The Mission Planning System converts approved imaging demand and spacecraft constraints into executable activity plans for routine operations.
S012: The Command Validation Gateway provides the formal barrier between planning outputs and command release, and it enforces rule checks before commands are made available for uplink.
S013: The Telemetry Ingest Service receives spacecraft telemetry from scheduled contacts and makes it available to operations, engineering analysis, and downstream processing functions.
S014: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine orbit maintenance by processing tracking inputs and producing controlled orbit knowledge for planning and product generation.
S015: The Product Quality Service performs automated and analyst-supported checks on generated products before they are exposed through operational dissemination channels.
S016: The Primary Processing Cluster is the nominal production environment for standard mission products, while the Backup Processing Cluster is maintained for resilience and controlled failover.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
{"summary":"Sentinel Vale is an Earth-observation mission providing routine land, coastal, and cryosphere imaging products with predictable latency and documented data quality. Ground segment purposes: plan spacecraft activities, acquire mission data, maintain safe spacecraft operations, generate user products, preserve mission records, and provide controlled service access. Spacecraft, launch segment, and external user processing environments are outside its boundary, except required operational interfaces.
Ground segment elements and responsibilities:
• Mission Control Center (alias Bluebell, for local voice coordination only): authority for real-time spacecraft operations, pass supervision, anomaly response, and release of validated command activities.
• Flight Dynamics Facility: provides orbit analysis, maneuver planning support, access prediction, and navigation products to other ground functions.
• Payload Processing Facility: operational environment for payload data processing, calibration control, product assessment, and distribution staging.
• Network Control System: monitors communications availability, routes operational traffic, and provides ground-connectivity status awareness.
• Mission Planning System: converts approved imaging demand and spacecraft constraints into executable activity plans for routine operations.
• Command Validation Gateway: formal barrier between planning outputs and command release; enforces rule checks before commands become available for uplink.
• Telemetry Ingest Service: receives spacecraft telemetry from scheduled contacts and makes it available to operations, engineering analysis, and downstream processing functions.
• Orbit Determination Engine: processes tracking inputs and produces controlled orbit knowledge for planning and product generation, supporting routine orbit maintenance.
• Product Quality Service: performs automated and analyst-supported checks on generated products before operational dissemination.
• Primary Processing Cluster: nominal production environment for standard mission products.
• Backup Processing Cluster: maintained for resilience and controlled failover.
• Long Term Archive; User Services Portal.
Controlled operational assets within the boundary: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna."}
